site.title: Hollyhock
site.tagline: Flowers from Chatsworth Road, delivered by bike

posts.title: Nkechi and Tom, Round Chapel, June
posts.content: A pink and silver bouquet with garden roses, freesias and brunia, and jam jars of sweet peas down two long tables. Photographs by Ama Boateng.

posts.title: Priya and Joe, a pub garden in Walthamstow
posts.content: Forty guests, one very old apple tree and a bouquet of lisianthus, astrantia and roses. Photographs by Marek Zielinski.

posts.title: Carnations are back and we are not sorry
posts.content: They last two weeks, they come in colours nobody else sells, and they cost less than a coffee a stem. We have 300 in the shop this week.

posts.title: Ellie and Sam, Clapton, September
posts.content: Orange and cream roses with rosehips and dahlias from Rosa's allotment. Photographs by Ama Boateng.

posts.title: Why we stopped using floral foam
posts.content: Foam is a plastic that breaks into dust and never goes away. Everything we make now sits in water, moss or scrunched chicken wire. It takes longer. It is worth it.

posts.title: Dahlias from the allotment, August to October
posts.content: Rosa grows about 60 dahlia plants on a plot in Walthamstow. They go into bouquets from August until the first frost.
